rows.regime_label: Domestic B2B structured electronic invoicing
rows.bound_party: Taxable persons established in Belgium supplying goods or services to another VAT-identified taxable person. Excluded by the law itself: taxable persons subject to the flat-rate scheme of Article 56 of the VAT Code, and bankrupt taxable persons.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test. The obligation binds every established taxable person in scope regardless of turnover or headcount, which makes Belgium the strictest of the 2026 cohort for small companies — there is no small-company deferral to wait for.
rows.format_name: Peppol BIS Billing (UBL), default standard
rows.format_version: 3.0.21 mandatory on the Peppol network from 2026-08-17
rows.format_note: The law requires a structured electronic form permitting automatic processing and compliant with EN 16931-1 and CEN/TS 16931-2. The implementing royal decree sets Peppol BIS Billing in UBL syntax, transmitted over the Peppol network, as the default standard; parties may agree an alternative format provided it still complies with the European standard. The version figure is the OpenPeppol release calendar, verified separately at docs.peppol.eu/poacc/billing/3.0/release-notes/ — Peppol BIS Billing 3.0.21 was published 2026-05-20 and became mandatory 2026-08-17, superseding 3.0.20. Belgian law does not itself name a Peppol version, so the version moves on OpenPeppol's schedule, not Belgium's.
rows.tolerance_note: Penalty tolerance only — not a postponement of the obligation. FPS Finance will not apply penalties for offences relating to the new e-invoicing obligation during the first three months of 2026 where the enterprise can show it took reasonable steps to comply, including where it lacks the technical means to send structured electronic invoices or its software cannot yet issue a valid one. FPS Finance states explicitly that "under no circumstances" will a general postponement be granted.
rows.legal_instrument: Loi du 6 février 2024 modifiant le Code de la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée et le Code des impôts sur les revenus 1992 en ce qui concerne l'introduction de l'obligation de facturation électronique, amending Article 53 of the VAT Code (Moniteur belge, 20 February 2024, numac 2024001635).
rows.source_title: Loi du 6 février 2024 — consolidated text as published in the Moniteur belge of 20 February 2024 (numac 2024001635), ejustice.just.fgov.be
rows.confidence_note: Gazette text read directly on 2026-10-07: the 1 January 2026 entry into force, the Article 56 and bankruptcy exclusions, the Article 44 and Article 135(1) scope carve-outs, and the EN 16931-1 / CEN/TS 16931-2 standard reference. The tolerance window and its penalties-only character were read the same day on the official einvoice.belgium.be portal (FPS Finance / BOSA). finances.belgium.be served a CAPTCHA to this host and was not used.
unknowns: The implementing royal decree that designates Peppol BIS Billing (UBL) as the default standard was not read directly; the format designation here is taken from the gazette's standard reference plus secondary description of the decree. The decree's own text, and whether it pins a Peppol BIS version, is unconfirmed.

Treatment of non-established taxable persons merely VAT-registered in Belgium is not recorded. The law binds persons "established in Belgium"; whether a foreign-established but Belgian-VAT-registered supplier is in or out is not established here.
rows.notes: Entry into force was conditional on EU Council authorisation under Article 395 of Directive 2006/112/EC. Out of scope per the law: supplies exempt under Article 44 of the VAT Code, and certain cross-border supplies under Article 135(1)(a)-(g) of Directive 2006/112/EC. VAT units are subject to different rules.

rows.regime_label: Domestic B2B structured electronic invoicing
rows.bound_party: Taxable persons established in Belgium receiving B2B supplies, excluding those subject to the flat-rate scheme of Article 56 of the VAT Code and bankrupt taxable persons.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test; applies regardless of turnover or headcount.
rows.format_name: Peppol BIS Billing (UBL), default standard
rows.format_version: 3.0.21 mandatory on the Peppol network from 2026-08-17
rows.format_note: Must be able to receive an EN 16931-compliant structured invoice. Peppol BIS Billing (UBL) over the Peppol network is the default standard; an alternative EN 16931-compliant format may be agreed between the parties.
rows.tolerance_note: Same penalty tolerance as the issuing duty. FPS Finance names inability to receive structured electronic invoices as a covered offence for the first three months of 2026. The obligation itself is not postponed.
rows.legal_instrument: Loi du 6 février 2024 modifiant le Code de la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée et le Code des impôts sur les revenus 1992 (Moniteur belge, 20 February 2024, numac 2024001635).
rows.source_title: Loi du 6 février 2024 — consolidated text as published in the Moniteur belge of 20 February 2024 (numac 2024001635), ejustice.just.fgov.be
rows.confidence_note: Gazette text read directly on 2026-10-07; tolerance read the same day on the official einvoice.belgium.be portal, which explicitly lists inability to receive among the tolerated offences.
unknowns: Whether a recipient may refuse a compliant structured invoice, or must accept one sent in an agreed alternative format, is not recorded.
rows.notes: Recorded separately from the issuing duty because "must I be able to receive yet?" is a different question from "must I issue yet?", even where the dates coincide. Same scope exclusions as BE-e-invoicing-b2b-issue-all.

rows.regime_label: Domestic B2B electronic invoicing (E-Rechnung)
rows.bound_party: Domestic entrepreneurs issuing an invoice for a supply to another domestic entrepreneur's business, whose total turnover (Gesamtumsatz, § 19 Abs. 2 UStG) in the preceding calendar year exceeded EUR 800,000.
rows.threshold_basis: Gesamtumsatz as defined in § 19 Abs. 2 UStG, of the entrepreneur issuing the invoice.
rows.threshold_definition: § 27 Abs. 38 UStG extends the tolerance to 31 December 2027 only "wenn der Gesamtumsatz (§ 19 Absatz 2) des die Rechnung ausstellenden Unternehmers im vorangegangenen Kalenderjahr nicht mehr als 800 000 Euro" betragen hat. This row is the cohort that fails that test, i.e. prior-year turnover above EUR 800,000, for whom the tolerance ends a year earlier.
rows.format_name: XRechnung, or ZUGFeRD (EN 16931-compliant profiles)
rows.format_version: ZUGFeRD 2.0.1 or later; XRechnung (current published version)
rows.format_note: BMF FAQ Q7: XRechnung and ZUGFeRD from version 2.0.1 satisfy the VAT requirements, excluding the MINIMUM and BASIC-WL profiles. Another format may be agreed between the parties if the UStG-required data can be extracted correctly and completely from it, which keeps EDI procedures such as EDIFACT usable.
rows.tolerance_note: From 1 Jan 2025 to 31 Dec 2026 any issuer may issue a "sonstige Rechnung" instead of an e-invoice. Paper is always permitted; another electronic format such as a PDF by e-mail requires the recipient's consent. Separately, a non-conforming EDI procedure may be used until 31 December 2027 even by this cohort (BMF FAQ Q11).
rows.legal_instrument: § 14 Abs. 2 Nr. 1 UStG; transitional rule § 27 Abs. 38 UStG (Wachstumschancengesetz).
rows.source_title: § 27 Abs. 38 Umsatzsteuergesetz — consolidated text, gesetze-im-internet.de (BMJ / Bundesanzeiger Verlag)
rows.confidence_note: Statutory text of § 27 Abs. 38 UStG read directly on 2026-10-07, including the EUR 800,000 figure and the "vorangegangenes Kalenderjahr" measurement period. Cross-checked against BMF FAQ (Stand März 2026) Q11, which states the same dates in plain language.
rows.notes: Date is driven by when the supply is carried out (Zeitpunkt des Umsatzes), not when the invoice is raised: § 27 Abs. 38 UStG frames the tolerance as applying to a supply "nach dem 31. Dezember 2024 und vor dem 1. Januar 2027 ausgeführten Umsatz".

Tested per year, so an entrepreneur crossing EUR 800,000 in 2026 loses the extra year for 2027 supplies.

rows.format_note: Same format set as the above-threshold cohort. BMF FAQ Q7: XRechnung and ZUGFeRD from version 2.0.1, excluding the MINIMUM and BASIC-WL profiles.

rows.regime_label: Domestic B2B electronic invoicing (E-Rechnung)
rows.bound_party: Every domestic entrepreneur (inländischer Unternehmer, § 2 UStG) acting in a business capacity, including small businesses (Kleinunternehmer), freelancers, and persons making only exempt supplies such as residential landlords and doctors.
rows.threshold_definition: No size, turnover or headcount threshold. BMF FAQ Q12: "Es sind keine Ausnahmen vorgesehen" — no exemptions are provided. Kleinunternehmer are exempt from issuing e-invoices but must still be able to receive them.
rows.format_name: EN 16931-compliant structured electronic invoice
rows.format_note: No specific transmission channel is prescribed. BMF FAQ Q8 and Q12: holding an e-mail inbox is sufficient to satisfy the receiving obligation ("Dazu reicht bereits ein E-Mail-Postfach aus").
rows.tolerance_note: No transition period applies to receiving. The 1 Jan 2025 – 31 Dec 2026 tolerance in § 27 Abs. 38 UStG covers the issuing of invoices only, not their receipt (BMF FAQ Q11, Q12).
rows.legal_instrument: § 14 Abs. 1 and Abs. 2 Nr. 1 UStG as recast by the Wachstumschancengesetz, for supplies carried out after 31 December 2024. Administrative interpretation: BMF-Schreiben of 15 October 2024 (BStBl I S. 1320) and 15 October 2025.
rows.source_title: Bundesministerium der Finanzen — Fragen und Antworten zur Einführung der obligatorischen E-Rechnung zum 1. Januar 2025 (Stand: März 2026)
rows.confidence_note: BMF FAQ read directly on 2026-10-07; page carries "Stand: März 2026" and is dated 23.03.2026. Questions 8 and 12 state the receiving obligation and the absence of exemptions. Statutory definition cross-read in § 14 Abs. 1 UStG.
rows.notes: This is the row most German small vendors get wrong: they are not obliged to issue until 2027 or 2028, but they have been obliged to be able to receive since 1 January 2025, with no grace period.

rows.regime_label: Facturación electrónica obligatoria entre empresarios y profesionales
rows.bound_party: Empresarios y profesionales whose volume of operations exceeded EUR 8,000,000 in the immediately preceding calendar year.
rows.threshold_basis: Volumen de operaciones calculated in accordance with article 121 of Ley 37/1992 (the Spanish VAT Act)
rows.threshold_period: el año natural inmediato anterior — the immediately preceding calendar year
rows.threshold_definition: Disposición final cuarta of Real Decreto 238/2026 phases the regime from the entry into force of the ministerial order developing the public invoicing solution: 12 months for empresarios y profesionales whose volume of operations, calculated per article 121 of Ley 37/1992, exceeded EUR 8,000,000 in the immediately preceding calendar year; 24 months for everyone else. Unlike Poland's fixed 2024 reference year, this is a rolling prior-year test.
rows.format_name: UBL (reference syntax for the public solution)
rows.format_note: Real Decreto 238/2026 permits CII, UBL, EDIFACT and Facturae. For the public invoicing solution specifically, UBL is the reference syntax: Anexo I of Orden HAC/1028/2026 is titled "Contenido y estructura de los campos de la factura electrónica conforme al modelo UBL y la EN 16931". No UBL version number is stated in the order's Anexo I heading as read, so the version is an open unknown rather than an omission.
rows.legal_instrument: Ley 18/2022, de 28 de septiembre, de creación y crecimiento de empresas, art. 12 (amending art. 2 bis of Ley 56/2007); Real Decreto 238/2026, de 25 de marzo (BOE-A-2026-7295), disposición final cuarta; Orden HAC/1028/2026, de 2 de octubre (BOE-A-2026-20587), disposición final única.
rows.source_title: Orden HAC/1028/2026, de 2 de octubre, por la que se regula la solución pública de facturación electrónica — BOE núm. 247, 5 October 2026, disposición núm. 20587 (boe.es)
rows.confidence_note: Two primary sources read on 2026-10-07. Orden HAC/1028/2026 retrieved as the BOE PDF and its text extracted: disposición final única states the order "entrará en vigor el día siguiente al de su publicación en el Boletín Oficial del Estado, dándose inicio al cómputo de los plazos previstos en la disposición final octava de la Ley 18/2022 ... y en las disposiciones transitorias primera a tercera y disposición final cuarta, del Real Decreto 238/2026". Published 5 October 2026, so in force 6 October 2026. Real Decreto 238/2026 read on boe.es for the 12/24-month periods, the EUR 8,000,000 threshold and the article 121 Ley 37/1992 basis. The row is `reported` and not `verified` because mandatory_from is OUR arithmetic (6 October 2026 + 12 months), not a date either instrument prints.
unknowns: Whether the 12-month period expires on 2027-10-06 or 2027-10-05 depends on how article 30 of Ley 39/2015 computes a period expressed in months from the date of entry into force. This is a legal-interpretation question, not a sourcing question — escalated to Odysseus. The date here is the later of the two readings.
No UBL version number was found in Anexo I of the order as read.
Whether the receiving obligation starts on the same dates as issuing is not established — see ES-e-invoicing-b2b-receive-all.
rows.notes: Commercially the freshest row in the dataset: before 6 October 2026 the Spanish dates could not be computed at all, because the phase-in was expressed as a period running from a ministerial order that had not been published. Any competitor snapshot taken before 5 October 2026 still shows Spain as undated.

rows.legal_instrument: Ley 18/2022, de 28 de septiembre, art. 12 (amending art. 2 bis of Ley 56/2007); Real Decreto 238/2026, de 25 de marzo; Orden HAC/1028/2026, de 2 de octubre.

rows.regime_label: Structured electronic invoicing for intra-Community supplies (ViDA)
rows.bound_party: Taxable persons obliged to issue an invoice for a transaction caught by the reporting obligations in Title XI, Chapter 6 of Directive 2006/112/EC - in substance the intra- Community transactions listed in the new Art. 262(1). The new Art. 218(2) reads "For the purposes of this Directive, invoices shall be issued as electronic invoices. However, Member States may accept documents or messages on paper or in electronic formats other than electronic invoices for transactions not subject to the reporting obligations laid down in Chapter 6." So the paper option survives only outside Chapter 6; for reportable intra-Community transactions the structured electronic invoice becomes the only invoice.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test. The trigger is the transaction type, not the size of the business: any taxable person identified for VAT purposes making a transaction listed in the new Art. 262(1) is in scope regardless of turnover or headcount.
rows.format_name: EN 16931-1 semantic data model, carried in a syntax from the published list
rows.format_note: The new Art. 218(3) reads "Electronic invoices shall comply with the European standard on electronic invoicing and the list of its syntaxes pursuant to Directive 2014/55/EU. Member States may allow the use of other standards for electronic invoices relating to supplies of goods and services within their territory, other than those referred to in Article 262 of this Directive." The other-standards latitude is therefore domestic only - it is not available for the intra-Community transactions this row covers. The standard and syntax list are those published by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2017/1870: EN 16931-1:2017 and CEN/TS 16931-2:2017. The new definition in Art. 217 requires a structured electronic format allowing automated processing at least for the data referred to in Arts. 262 and 271b, which is what makes a hybrid invoice acceptable if the reportable data are in the structured part.
rows.legal_instrument: Council Directive (EU) 2025/516, Art. 5 points (4) and (5) (replacing Arts. 217 and 218 of Directive 2006/112/EC) and Art. 6(5)
rows.source_title: Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 on VAT rules for the digital age (OJ L series, 2025/516, 25.3.2025)
rows.confidence_note: Read on 2026-10-07 from http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32025L0516 (Accept: application/xhtml+xml, Accept-Language: eng). Art. 6(5) reads "Member States shall adopt and publish, by 30 June 2030, the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with Article 5 ... They shall apply those measures from 1 July 2030", which is the value in mandatory_from. The replacement Arts. 217 and 218 at Art. 5 points (4) and (5), and the replacement Art. 222 first paragraph at Art. 5 point (8), were read verbatim.
unknowns: No format cutover date is fixed for a future revision of EN 16931-1. Art. 218(3) cites the standard by reference to Directive 2014/55/EU, so a CEN revision published before 2030 would change what compliance means without any date appearing in this directive.

Art. 5 point (3) lets Member States make possession of a compliant electronic invoice a substantive condition for deducting or reclaiming VAT. Whether a given Member State takes that option is national law and is not recorded here.
The accreditation or assurance measures the new Art. 218(4) requires of Member States, and whether they will fall on issuers or on service providers, are not fixed by the directive.
rows.notes: Paired with Art. 5 point (8), which replaces the first paragraph of Art. 222: for supplies under Art. 138 and for supplies where VAT is payable by the customer under Arts. 194-197, "an invoice shall be issued no later than 10 days following the chargeable event" (also 10 days from receipt of a payment on account, and summary invoices no later than 10 days after the end of the month they cover). That 10-day clock is the operational change most small vendors will feel, and it starts on the same date as this row.

rows.regime_label: Domestic B2B electronic invoicing - Member-State option (ViDA)
rows.bound_party: Member States, not taxable persons. Art. 1(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/516 adds to Art. 218 of Directive 2006/112/EC: "By way of derogation from the first paragraph of this Article, Member States may, in accordance with the conditions they lay down, require taxable persons established within their territory to issue electronic invoices for supplies of goods and services within their territory, other than those referred to in Article 262." Art. 1(3) adds to Art. 232 that a Member State exercising that option may provide that use of such invoices is not subject to the recipient's acceptance. This row records the EU-level enabling date only. A duty on a business arises solely from the national act that uses it.
rows.threshold_definition: The EU provision sets no size test. Art. 1(2) hands the Member State the conditions ("in accordance with the conditions they lay down"), which is where every national turnover and headcount band in this dataset comes from.
rows.format_name: Set by the Member State
rows.format_note: Arts. 1(2) and 1(3) impose no format: the Member State lays down the conditions. The EN 16931 requirement arrives later, with the Art. 5 replacement of Art. 218 from 1 July 2030 (see EU-e-invoicing-b2b-issue-intra-community-structured), and even then the new Art. 218(3) lets Member States allow other standards for domestic supplies.
rows.legal_instrument: Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 of 11 March 2025 amending Directive 2006/112/EC as regards VAT rules for the digital age, Arts. 1(2), 1(3), 6(1) and 7
rows.source_title: Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 on VAT rules for the digital age (OJ L series, 2025/516, 25.3.2025)
rows.confidence_note: Full English text of Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 read on 2026-10-07 from the Publications Office cellar, http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32025L0516 with Accept: application/xhtml+xml and Accept-Language: eng. Art. 6(1) reads "Member States may apply the laws, regulations and administrative provisions regarding Article 1, points 2 and 3 from 14 April 2025", which is the value in mandatory_from. Arts. 1(2), 1(3) and 7 read verbatim; the OJ masthead on the text read is "L series, 2025/516, 25.3.2025".
unknowns: This is an enabling date for Member States, not a date on which any taxable person must issue an electronic invoice. Do not render it as a company obligation or as an answer on a size-band page.

The directive text does not itself state that an Art. 395 authorisation ceases to be required in order to mandate domestic e-invoicing. What the text establishes is the enabling provisions and their date. The only Art. 395 references in the text read are recital (24) and Art. 6(5), both about pre-existing domestic real-time reporting systems.
Whether Art. 395 authorisations granted to individual Member States before this directive remain in force, and on what terms, was not established from the text read.
What happens to the EU enabling date in a Member State that has not legislated is outside this row: absence of a national row in this dataset means not yet recorded, not "no duty".
rows.notes: The hinge under every national domestic B2B mandate in this dataset. Art. 232 of Directive 2006/112/EC made the use of an electronic invoice subject to the recipient's acceptance; Art. 1(3) of 2025/516 lets a Member State that exercises the new Art. 218 option disapply that acceptance requirement for recipients established in its territory. Art. 7 sets entry into force at the twentieth day after OJ publication, and the OJ carrying the text is dated 25 March 2025, which is consistent with the 14 April 2025 date Art. 6(1) prints.

rows.regime_label: Public-procurement electronic invoicing (Directive 2014/55/EU)
rows.bound_party: Member States, which must ensure that contracting authorities and contracting entities receive and process electronic invoices (Art. 7). The duty lands on the public buyer, not on the supplier: the directive creates no obligation on an economic operator to invoice electronically. "Contracting authorities", "sub-central contracting authorities", "central purchasing body" and "contracting entities" take their Art. 2 meanings by reference to Directives 2009/81/EC, 2014/23/EU, 2014/24/EU and 2014/25/EU. Scope is electronic invoices issued under contracts to which those four directives apply (Art. 1), excluding contracts declared secret or requiring special security measures under Directive 2009/81/EC.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test of any kind. The obligation attaches to the status of the buyer as a contracting authority or contracting entity, not to turnover, headcount or contract value. Art. 3(1) and recitals 41-42 require that SMEs' and smaller authorities' needs be taken into account when the standard is drawn up and when support is offered; that is a design criterion, not an exemption.
rows.format_name: EN 16931-1 semantic data model, carried in a syntax from the published list
rows.format_note: The Art. 3(2) reference was published by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2017/1870, OJ L 266, 17.10.2017, p. 19. Its Art. 1 publishes "EN 16931-1:2017, Electronic invoicing - Part 1: Semantic data model of the core elements of an electronic invoice" together with the syntax list "CEN/TS 16931-2:2017, Part 2". The Annex names exactly two syntaxes: UN/CEFACT Cross Industry Invoice XML as specified in XML Schemas 16B (SCRDM - CII), and UBL invoice and credit note messages as defined in ISO/IEC 19845:2015. CEN issued both deliverables on 28 June 2017. Any later CEN amendment to EN 16931-1:2017 was not read.

rows.regime_label: Domestic digital reporting - convergence of pre-existing national systems (ViDA)
rows.bound_party: Member States operating a domestic transaction-based reporting system, and through them the taxable persons established or identified for VAT purposes in their territory. Domestic reporting stays optional for the Member State: the new Art. 271a reads "Member States may require that taxable persons established or identified for VAT purposes in their territory send electronically to their tax authorities data on the supplies of goods and services, other than those referred to in Article 262, made within their territory" to themselves or to other taxable persons, and Art. 271a(4) lets a Member State limit the obligation to certain categories of taxable person or types of transaction. What stops being optional is the shape: a state that requires domestic reporting must run it on the harmonised Art. 271b model - per transaction, at invoice issuance, or within 5 days for self-billing and for the acquisition side.
rows.threshold_definition: The EU provision sets no size test, but explicitly permits one: Art. 271b(4) lets a Member State limit the scope to certain categories of taxable person. National thresholds for domestic reporting are therefore lawful and belong on that country's rows, not here.
rows.format_name: Member State's choice, constrained to interoperate with EN 16931
rows.format_note: No single format. The new Art. 271b(3) requires Member States to allow transmission of data from EN 16931-compliant electronic invoices, and permits other data formats "provided that the other data formats ensure interoperability with that standard". So the national format is open but EN 16931-tethered; there is no EU version or cutover date to record.
rows.tolerance_note: Art. 6(5) second subparagraph: a Member State that, on 1 January 2024, already had a domestic digital real-time transaction-based reporting obligation in place - or had been granted an Art. 395 authorisation before that date allowing one, or, where no authorisation was needed, had adopted national legislation before that date providing for one - need only apply the Art. 5 point (5) measures on Art. 218 and the Art. 5 point (19) measures on Arts. 271a and 271b "by 1 January 2035, in so far as domestic electronic invoicing and reporting are concerned". It is a grandfathering window for the state's existing system, not a grace period for businesses: the national duty keeps running in its current form throughout. The window can be pushed further - if the Art. 271c interim report (due by 31 March 2033) finds shortcomings, the Commission is to assess the need for further measures and may propose postponing the deadline.

It has to be established state by state against the three alternative tests in Art. 6(5) as they stood on 1 January 2024, and that determination has not been made for any country in this dataset yet.

The 2035 date is conditional. Art. 6(5) and recital (24) both allow it to be postponed if the Art. 271c interim report (due 31 March 2033) reveals shortcomings, so it is the current ceiling rather than a settled date.

Art. 5 point (20) amends Art. 273 to bar new additional general transaction-based reporting obligations beyond Chapter 6, while letting pre-2024 systems run "until they implement" a compliant system. How that interacts with the 2035 date for a state that converges early was not resolved from the text read.
format_version is null by nature, not by omission: the directive sets an interoperability requirement rather than naming a format, so there is no EU-level version to track.

Italy's SdI and comparable pre-2024 systems sit inside this window. The row records the EU-level date and the window only; the per-country consequence has to be sourced from each national instrument, and none of those determinations are in the dataset yet.

rows.regime_label: Intra-Community digital reporting requirements (ViDA)
rows.bound_party: Every taxable person identified for VAT purposes, for the transactions listed in the new Art. 262(1): Art. 138(1) and 138(2)(c) supplies and transfers of goods; intra-Community acquisitions under Art. 20 and transactions treated as such under Arts. 21-22; and non- exempt supplies and acquisitions where the customer is liable for VAT under Arts. 194-197 or 204. Reporting runs per transaction, not per period: data go in at the time the invoice is issued or should have been issued (new Art. 263(1)), within 5 days where the customer self-bills, and within 5 days of receiving the invoice on the acquisition side (new Art. 263(2)). Member States may waive the acquisition-side legs under Art. 262(4), and taxable persons in the Title XII Chapter 6 Section 5 special scheme are carved out of the own-goods transfer legs by Art. 262(3).
rows.threshold_definition: No size test. Identification for VAT purposes plus a listed transaction is the whole test; the Art. 262(3) and 262(4) carve-outs turn on scheme and Member-State choice, not on size.

Čl. 38(1)(1) binds "porezni obveznik sa sjedištem, prebivalištem ili uobičajenim boravištem u tuzemstvu koji je upisan u registar obveznika PDV-a". Čl. 80 brings čl. 33–43 into force on 2026-01-01 and carves out only čl. 38 st. 1 toč. 2. i 3. and čl. 54–56 to 2027-01-01, which is what puts category 1 on the earlier date. The gazette was read directly because a first pass over the HTML rendering returned a staging that the gazette text does not support.
unknowns: The version of the Porezna uprava "Tehnička specifikacija osnovne uporabe eRačuna s proširenjima" (the Croatian CIUS) is not pinned by the Act and was not established. Since čl. 2(9) makes that specification part of the binding "EU norma", its version is a live compliance variable that no gazette will announce.

Whether a taxable person not established in Croatia but registered for Croatian VAT is inside čl. 38(1)(1) is not resolved: the provision requires both VAT registration AND a domestic seat, residence or habitual residence, but the treatment of a non-established VAT registrant is not spelled out.
The pravilnik under čl. 32 (ministerial implementing regulation, due within 90 days of commencement per čl. 77) has not been read and may carry further format or process detail.
rows.notes: Scope limits worth knowing. Čl. 33(3): the eRačun provisions apply only to DOMESTIC transactions. Čl. 33(2): they do not apply to supplies under contracts protected by a prescribed degree of secrecy or requiring special security measures. Čl. 39: a transaction paid in cash or by card for which a receipt was issued and fiscalised under čl. 15 may be exempt from issuing an eRačun — and where that route is used an eRačun must NOT also be issued. Čl. 38(3) closes the obvious gap: an issuer who is exempt but issues an invoice anyway must issue it as an eRačun with all the duties attached. Čl. 35: issued and received eRačuni must be kept in original form for six years from the end of the year of issue.

rows.regime_label: HR Fiskalizacija 2.0 — eRačun in business between taxable persons
rows.bound_party: Every "primatelj eRačuna" as defined in čl. 2(24): (a) a taxable person established in Croatia and entered in the VAT register; (b) a non-VAT-registered payer of income tax on self-employment or of corporate income tax established in Croatia; (c) bodies of state administration, local and regional self-government units, and budgetary and extra-budgetary users in the Register who are not VAT-registered.
rows.threshold_basis: Any recipient of an eRačun under čl. 2(24) — VAT-registered or not
rows.threshold_definition: No size test and, critically, NO entity-class deferral on the receiving side. Čl. 41 falls inside the čl. 33–43 block that čl. 80 brings into force on 2026-01-01, and the čl. 80 carve-out to 2027-01-01 names only čl. 38 st. 1 toč. 2. i 3. (issuing) and čl. 54–56. So all three recipient categories must be able to receive from 2026-01-01, including the ones that do not have to issue until 2027-01-01.
rows.format_name: EU norma (EN 16931-1:2017 with the Croatian Porezna uprava extensions)
rows.format_note: Čl. 41 requires receipt "na način propisan člankom 37. ovoga Zakona" — čl. 37(1) routes exchange through access points (pristupne točke), which čl. 37(2) obliges to guarantee standardised formats, protocols and interoperability. Čl. 37(3) permits exchange by other technologies and procedures provided authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility are preserved, so the access-point route is the default rather than the only lawful channel. Čl. 38(4) requires the access point's identity to be proven by digital certificate with a mandatory OIB signing the message.
rows.legal_instrument: Zakon o fiskalizaciji ("Narodne novine" br. 89/2025), čl. 41, čl. 37, čl. 2(24), čl. 38(4); commencement under čl. 80.

The definition of primatelj eRačuna at čl. 2(24)(a)–(c) was read and covers all three entity categories. The 2026-01-01 date follows from čl. 80 listing čl. 33–43 for that date with no receiving-side carve-out.
unknowns: Croatian CIUS version not established — same gap as the issuing rows.

The list of authorised access points (pristupne točke) and whether a recipient must register with one by a specific date was not established; čl. 46 makes publication on the Lista identifikatora poreznih obveznika voluntary, which leaves open how an issuer discovers a recipient's address.
rows.notes: This is the row that bites first and the one most likely to be missed. A small non-VAT-registered Croatian trader has no duty to issue an eRačun until 2027-01-01 but must already be able to receive and fiscalise one from 2026-01-01, because its VAT-registered suppliers are obliged to send one from that date.

rows.regime_label: HR public procurement — eRačun in javnoj nabavi
rows.bound_party: Suppliers and service providers issuing invoices in public procurement procedures to Croatian contracting authorities and contracting entities.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test identified. Croatia went further than Directive 2014/55/EU requires: the directive obliges only the contracting authority to RECEIVE, whereas Croatia also obliges the supplier to ISSUE electronically, which is why this is recorded as a direction=issue row rather than only a receiving duty.
rows.format_name: EN 16931 (European standard on electronic invoicing)
rows.format_note: Format recorded from the standard that Directive 2014/55/EU requires and that čl. 2(9) of the 2025 Zakon o fiskalizaciji also adopts; the 2018 public-procurement act's own format provision and any Croatian CIUS version for B2G were not read. Note čl. 33(1) of the 2025 Act: the rules on issuing eRačune in public procurement apply mutatis mutandis to the B2B eRačun regime, so the two regimes are deliberately aligned.
rows.legal_instrument: Zakon o elektroničkom izdavanju računa u javnoj nabavi ("Narodne novine" br. 94/2018), transposing Directive 2014/55/EU. The gazette text was not read.
rows.source_title: Ministarstvo gospodarstva (Croatian Ministry of Economy), "Objavljen Zakon o elektroničkom izdavanju računa u javnoj nabavi"
rows.confidence_note: The Act's existence, its gazette reference (NN 94/2018), its entry into force on 2018-11-01 and the two operative dates (authorities receive from 2018-12-01, suppliers issue from 2019-07-01) are consistent across the Ministry of Economy's own announcement and Croatian practitioner sources read on 2026-10-07. The gazette text itself was not retrieved, so this is graded reported. Primary source supremacy: it becomes verified when NN 94/2018 is read, not because several sources agree.
unknowns: The gazette text of NN 94/2018 has not been read. The 2019-07-01 issuing date and the 2018-12-01 receiving date rest on the Ministry's announcement and secondary coverage, not on the statute.
Article numbers for the issuing duty and the format provision are not recorded.

Whether the 2025 Zakon o fiskalizaciji amended or displaced any part of the 2018 act was not checked; čl. 33(1) cross-refers to it rather than repealing it, and čl. 79 repeals only the old cash-fiscalisation act.
rows.notes: Croatia has had a working national e-invoicing channel since 2019, which is why the 2026 B2B mandate is a smaller step there than the same date would be elsewhere.

rows.regime_label: HR public procurement — eRačun in javnoj nabavi
rows.bound_party: Croatian contracting authorities and contracting entities, obliged to receive electronic invoices in public procurement.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test. The duty attaches to the contracting authority.
rows.format_name: EN 16931 (European standard on electronic invoicing)
rows.format_note: Core invoice model under EN 16931-1:2017. The 2018 act's own format provision was not read; no B2G Croatian CIUS version is recorded.
rows.legal_instrument: Zakon o elektroničkom izdavanju računa u javnoj nabavi ("Narodne novine" br. 94/2018), transposing Directive 2014/55/EU art. 7 and art. 11.
