rows.confidence_note: Receiving date of 2018-12-01 taken from the Ministry of Economy announcement and Croatian practitioner coverage read on 2026-10-07. Gazette text not read, so graded reported.
unknowns: NN 94/2018 gazette text not read; the 2018-12-01 date rests on secondary description.
Whether the receiving duty was staged between central and sub-central authorities, as Directive 2014/55/EU permits, is not recorded.
rows.notes: Recorded separately from the issuing duty because the dates differ by seven months, and a supplier reconstructing its 2019 position needs to know that authorities could already receive before suppliers were obliged to send.

rows.regime_label: HR Fiskalizacija 2.0 — fiscalisation of eRačuni to the Porezna uprava
rows.bound_party: The issuer of an eRačun, obliged under čl. 47 to carry out fiscalisation of the eRačun for every eRačun issued, by transmitting the prescribed čl. 48 data into the Sustav za fiskalizaciju.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test. Čl. 47 attaches to every issued eRačun. In practice the reporting duty is reached only once a party is obliged to issue, so the entity-class dates on the e-invoicing rows govern when this one starts to bite for a given business.
rows.format_name: Sustav za fiskalizaciju eRačuna data set (čl. 48)
rows.format_note: The Act prescribes the data to be delivered (čl. 48) rather than naming a published format with a version number, and the technical specification is left to the pravilnik under čl. 32, which the Minister of Finance must adopt within 90 days of commencement (čl. 77) and which has not been read. No version can honestly be recorded yet.
rows.legal_instrument: Zakon o fiskalizaciji ("Narodne novine" br. 89/2025), čl. 47, čl. 48, čl. 2(10); commencement under čl. 80.
rows.source_title: Zakon o fiskalizaciji, Narodne novine br. 89, 13 June 2025, act no. 1233 (official gazette PDF)
rows.confidence_note: Čl. 47 read verbatim on 2026-10-07: "Obvezu fiskalizacije eRačuna izdavatelj eRačuna i primatelj eRačuna dužni su provoditi za svaki izdani i zaprimljeni eRačun." Čl. 2(10) defines fiskalizacija eRačuna as delivering prescribed eRačun data into the Sustav za fiskalizaciju, covering both issuing and receiving. Čl. 47 sits in the čl. 47–57 block that čl. 80 brings into force on 2026-01-01.
unknowns: The deadline for transmitting the fiscalisation data — real-time, same-day, or within a stated window — was not established from the provisions read. For a reporting regime that is the most commercially important single parameter, and it is probably in the čl. 32 pravilnik.
The technical format and its version are not established pending the čl. 32 pravilnik.
rows.notes: Recorded as e-reporting rather than e-invoicing deliberately, the same call as Hungary. The duty here is to tell the Porezna uprava about the invoice, which is a different obligation from the duty to render the invoice in the EU norm. Croatia is unusual in running both at once from the same date, and in putting the reporting duty on the RECIPIENT as well as the issuer — see HR-e-reporting-receive-all.

rows.regime_label: HR Fiskalizacija 2.0 — fiscalisation of eRačuni to the Porezna uprava
rows.bound_party: The recipient of an eRačun, obliged under čl. 47 to carry out fiscalisation for every eRačun received. Čl. 51–53 additionally cover reporting of rejected and of paid eRačuni.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test. Every recipient under čl. 2(24) — including non-VAT-registered traders and public bodies that have no issuing duty until 2027-01-01 — must fiscalise what it receives from 2026-01-01.
rows.format_name: Sustav za fiskalizaciju eRačuna data set (čl. 48, čl. 51–53)
rows.format_note: As with the issuing side, the Act prescribes data rather than a versioned published format; the čl. 32 pravilnik carries the technical detail and has not been read.
rows.legal_instrument: Zakon o fiskalizaciji ("Narodne novine" br. 89/2025), čl. 47, čl. 48, čl. 51–53; commencement under čl. 80.
rows.source_title: Zakon o fiskalizaciji, Narodne novine br. 89, 13 June 2025, act no. 1233 (official gazette PDF)
rows.confidence_note: Čl. 47 read verbatim on 2026-10-07 and names the primatelj eRačuna alongside the izdavatelj as an obligor for every received eRačun. Čl. 80 places čl. 47–57 at 2026-01-01.
unknowns: Transmission deadline for recipient-side fiscalisation not established — same gap as the issuing row.
Whether rejection reporting under čl. 51–53 carries its own separate deadline was not established.
rows.notes: A buyer-side reporting duty is rare and expensive to implement, which makes it worth its own row rather than a footnote. A Croatian business that only receives invoices still has a reporting obligation from 2026-01-01.

rows.regime_label: HU public procurement — contracting authorities must receive e-invoices
rows.bound_party: Hungarian contracting authorities and contracting entities, obliged to receive and process electronic invoices conforming to the European standard in public procurement.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test. Directive 2014/55/EU binds contracting authorities irrespective of the supplier's size. Hungary is reported not to have taken the extra year that the directive allowed for sub-central authorities, so the 2019 date is reported to apply to all of them rather than only to central bodies — that is the specific point the unknowns flag.
rows.format_name: EN 16931 (European standard on electronic invoicing)
rows.format_note: Core invoice semantic data model under EN 16931-1:2017, in one of the syntaxes on the list published in the Official Journal. No Hungarian CIUS was identified; whether one exists was not checked.
rows.legal_instrument: Directive 2014/55/EU on electronic invoicing in public procurement, art. 7 and art. 11; reported to be transposed by 2018. évi LXXXIII. törvény amending 2015. évi CXLIII. törvény a közbeszerzésekről (Kbt.). The transposing provision was not read.
rows.source_title: European Commission, "eInvoicing in Hungary" (Digital Building Blocks country page)
rows.confidence_note: Taken from the European Commission's country page on 2026-10-07, which states that Hungarian public bodies must receive and process EN 16931-compliant e-invoices and that Hungary did not use the extra year available to sub-central authorities. The Commission's country page is a description of national law, not the national instrument, so it is secondary for this purpose and the row is graded reported. Primary source supremacy: this becomes verified when the Kbt. amendment is read on njt.hu, not before.
unknowns: The Hungarian transposing provision (the 2018. évi LXXXIII. törvény amendment to the Kbt.) has not been read. Both the 2019-04-18 date and the claim that sub-central authorities were not given until 2020-04-18 rest on secondary description.
Whether Hungarian contracting authorities are additionally obliged to receive via a specific channel or network is not recorded.
Whether suppliers to Hungarian public bodies have a matching duty to ISSUE electronically is not recorded; the directive imposes the receiving duty only.
rows.notes: Recorded as a separate regime from Online Számla on purpose. A Hungarian supplier invoicing a public body is in both: it must report the invoice data to NAV under e-reporting, and it may send an EN 16931 invoice that the authority must accept under this row. They are different duties with different formats and different dates, and collapsing them would be wrong.

rows.regime_label: HU Online Számla — real-time invoice data reporting (RTIR)
rows.bound_party: Every invoice issuer subject to the Hungarian VAT Act's invoicing rules, for every invoice, corrective invoice and cancelling invoice to which those rules apply — including invoices to private individuals, to foreign taxable persons, and invoices issued outside Hungary where Hungarian VAT arises.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test, and no per-invoice value test. The HUF 100,000 VAT floor that existed in the first phase was abolished on 2020-07-01 and the remaining customer-type restriction was abolished on 2021-01-04. Since then every invoice in scope of the Áfa tv. invoicing rules is reportable regardless of the issuer's size or the invoice's value.
rows.format_name: NAV Online Számla invoice data XML (XSD)
rows.format_note: Version 3.0 of the Online Invoice schema set (API, Data, Annulment, Metrics, plus the shared Common and invoiceBase XSDs) is the version the expanded reporting runs on; NAV's own changelog states the 3.0 features "can only be used from 04.01.2021" and that earlier use is rejected. Whether a 3.0.x point release is currently the one in force was not established — see unknowns. This is an XML reporting schema, not an invoice format: it does not have to be what the issuer sends the customer.
rows.tolerance_note: Penalty tolerance only, and only for the newly in-scope invoices. NAV: for the period 2021-01-04 to 2021-03-31 it imposed no default fine (mulasztási bírság) on taxable persons who failed to report, or misreported, the invoices that newly entered scope on 2021-01-04, subject to stated conditions. The reporting duty itself ran from 2021-01-04; only the fine was withheld. The tolerance did not extend to invoices already in scope before that date.
rows.legal_instrument: 2007. évi CXXVII. törvény az általános forgalmi adóról (VAT Act) § 158/A and Annex 10 (10. számú melléklet), read with §§ 169–172 and § 176; default-fine power under 2017. évi CL. törvény (Art.) § 229.
rows.source_title: NAV, "A számlakibocsátók számlaadat-szolgáltatásának 2021. január 4-től hatályos szabályai" (nav.gov.hu), published 2021-01-04
rows.confidence_note: NAV's own guidance page read on 2026-10-07. It cites Áfa tv. § 158/A and Annex 10, states that from 2021-01-04 data must be reported not only for invoices to customers registered as taxable persons in Hungary but for every invoice to which the Áfa tv. invoicing rules apply, and states the 2021-01-04 to 2021-03-31 fine-free window for the newly in-scope invoices. The 3.0 schema version and its 2021-01-04 activation were read from NAV's own schema changelog in the nav-gov-hu GitHub organisation.
unknowns: Whether a 3.0.x point release (rather than plain 3.0) is the version currently required was not established. NAV's GitHub release tags stop at API-2.0 and the 3.0 changelog lists no point releases, while secondary sources claim NAV withdrew 2.0 support on 2025-05-15 — a date that cannot be reconciled with 3.0 being mandatory since 2021 and was not confirmed against NAV.

Hungary's separate mandatory e-invoicing duty in the energy sector (electricity and gas supplied to non-residential customers) is not yet a row. It is a genuine e-invoicing mandate rather than reporting, so it needs its own regime row and its own source read.
Whether a non-established but Hungarian-VAT-registered supplier is inside the reporting duty is not recorded at row level.
rows.notes: Submission deadline depends on how the invoice is produced. From invoicing software: in XML over the machine-to-machine interface immediately on issue, without human intervention. From a pre-printed invoice book: within one calendar day of issue if the VAT charged is HUF 500,000 or more, otherwise within four calendar days. Reporting counts as performed only once the Online Számla system has received it and confirmed successful processing — a submitted-but-rejected file is an unperformed obligation, which is the detail that catches implementers out.

rows.regime_label: HU Online Számla — real-time invoice data reporting (RTIR)
rows.bound_party: Invoice issuers, for invoices issued to customers registered as taxable persons in Hungary — the scope of the regime between 2020-07-01 and 2021-01-03, retained as a historical row.
rows.threshold_basis: Customer is a taxable person registered in Hungary (belföldön nyilvántartásba vett áfaalany)
rows.threshold_definition: The test in this phase was on the customer, not on the supplier's size. From 2020-07-01 the HUF 100,000 VAT floor was removed and data had to be reported for every invoice issued to a Hungarian-registered taxable person whatever the VAT amount, which pulled reverse-charge and exempt supplies into scope for the first time. Invoices to private individuals and to foreign customers stayed out of scope until 2021-01-04.
rows.format_name: NAV Online Számla invoice data XML (XSD)
rows.format_note: This phase ran on schema 2.0; the 3.0 schema could not be used before 2021-01-04. Version number taken from NAV's published interface specification v2.0 and its API-2.0 release tag. Recorded for the audit trail — a buyer reconstructing a 2020 position needs the version that was actually in force then, not today's.
rows.legal_instrument: 2007. évi CXXVII. törvény az általános forgalmi adóról, § 10. számú melléklet, in the wording in force from 2020-07-01.
rows.source_title: NAV, "A számlakibocsátók számlaadat-szolgáltatásának 2021. január 4-től hatályos szabályai" (nav.gov.hu)
rows.confidence_note: The customer-type scope of this phase is established from the primary source — NAV's 2021-01-04 page states the pre-2021 position was that data were reported only for invoices to customers registered as taxable persons in Hungary. The 2020-07-01 commencement date itself is NOT in that page and was taken from secondary Hungarian practitioner coverage, so the row is graded reported rather than verified. Confidence labelling is not something to round up: the scope is primary, the date is not, and the lower of the two governs.
unknowns: The 2020-07-01 commencement date has not been read from a primary source. The amending act and the Annex 10 wording in force on that date were not retrieved.
rows.notes: Kept as a historical row rather than deleted. The change log is a product, and this is the row that tells a buyer being audited for 2020 which invoices they should have reported.

rows.regime_label: HU Online Számla — real-time invoice data reporting (RTIR)
rows.bound_party: Invoice issuers, for invoices to Hungarian-registered taxable persons carrying HUF 100,000 or more of charged VAT — the scope of the regime from 2018-07-01 to 2020-06-30, retained as a historical row.
rows.threshold_basis: VAT charged (áthárított adó) on the individual invoice
rows.threshold_period: per invoice — not a period measure
rows.threshold_definition: A PER-INVOICE test, not a size band on the company: an invoice between Hungarian taxable persons was reportable if the VAT charged on it reached HUF 100,000. Schema v1 has no per-invoice threshold_type, so `revenue_or_fees` is used and `threshold_period` says explicitly that this is not measured over a period. Do not band a company against this figure. Abolished on 2020-07-01.
rows.format_name: NAV Online Számla invoice data XML (XSD)
rows.format_note: The system went live on 2018-07-01 on schema 1.x; NAV's release tags record API-1.0 as the "first production release since 01-07-2018" and API-1.1 as an upgrade, with API-2.0 arriving later. Which of 1.0 / 1.1 applied on a given date in that phase was not pinned down.
rows.legal_instrument: 2007. évi CXXVII. törvény az általános forgalmi adóról, § 10. számú melléklet, in the wording in force from 2018-07-01.
rows.source_title: NAV, "A számlakibocsátók számlaadat-szolgáltatásának 2021. január 4-től hatályos szabályai" (nav.gov.hu)
rows.confidence_note: Phase recorded from secondary Hungarian practitioner coverage of the 2018 go-live and of the 2020-07-01 removal of the HUF 100,000 floor. NAV's 2021-01-04 page, which is the primary source held for this jurisdiction, describes the pre-2021 scope but does not state the 2018 date or the HUF 100,000 figure, so this row cannot be graded verified.
unknowns: Neither the 2018-07-01 commencement date nor the HUF 100,000 VAT figure has been read from a primary source.
The exact schema version in force at go-live (1.0 vs 1.1) is not established.
rows.notes: Historical row. Both this phase and the 2020-07-01 phase are closed, so neither binds anyone today; they exist because an audit of an open earlier year is exactly when a buyer needs to know what the rule was then.

rows.regime_label: Electronic invoicing via the Sistema di Interscambio (SdI)
rows.bound_party: Taxpayers applying the Italian flat-rate regime (regime forfetario, L. 190/2014 art. 1 cc. 54–89) who were not already required to issue electronic invoices from 1 July 2022 — i.e. those whose revenue or fees in the preceding year, pro-rated to a full year, did not exceed EUR 25,000.
rows.threshold_basis: Ricavi conseguiti ovvero compensi percepiti, ragguagliati ad anno (revenue earned or fees received, pro-rated to a full year).
rows.threshold_period: the year preceding the relevant commencement date
rows.threshold_definition: DL 36/2022 art. 18 c. 3 brought the obligation forward to 1 July 2022 for forfetario taxpayers who "nell'anno precedente abbiano conseguito ricavi ovvero percepito compensi, ragguagliati ad anno, superiori a euro 25.000". This row is the residual cohort at or below that figure, for whom the obligation runs from 1 January 2024 "a prescindere dall'entità dei ricavi conseguiti o compensi percepiti" — irrespective of revenue. So the threshold selects the commencement date, and from 1 January 2024 it no longer screens anyone out.
rows.format_name: FatturaPA XML, transmitted through the Sistema di Interscambio (SdI)
rows.format_note: National format, not EN 16931. Technical specifications v1.9 usable from 1 April 2025; v1.9.1 usable from 15 May 2026. Agenzia delle Entrate has published no date on which v1.9 ceases to be accepted by the SdI, so v1.9 is recorded as the current floor rather than v1.9.1.
rows.legal_instrument: DL 30 aprile 2022 n. 36, art. 18 cc. 2–3, which repealed the exemption in art. 1 c. 3 of D.Lgs. 5 agosto 2015 n. 127. Administrative interpretation: Agenzia delle Entrate Circolare n. 32/E of 5 December 2023.
rows.source_title: Decreto-legge 30 aprile 2022 n. 36, art. 18 — consolidated text in force, Normattiva (Istituto Poligrafico e Zecca dello Stato)
rows.confidence_note: Commi 2 and 3 of DL 36/2022 art. 18 read directly from the Normattiva consolidated "vigente" text on 2026-10-07, confirming both dates and the EUR 25,000 / ragguagliati ad anno wording. FatturaPA version dates read directly from the two Agenzia delle Entrate specification pages on 2026-10-07.
unknowns: Whether any penalty-free grace period applied to the 1 January 2024 cohort. The 1 July 2022 cohort had one under DL 36/2022 art. 18 c. 3 for the third quarter of 2022; no equivalent for 2024 was located in this pass.

The 'contribuenti minimi' (DL 98/2011 art. 27) and amateur sports bodies were covered by the same repealed exemption in art. 1 c. 3 D.Lgs. 127/2015, but were not separately verified here and have no row yet.
The date on which FatturaPA specification v1.9 stops being accepted by the SdI. Agenzia delle Entrate states only that v1.9.1 is 'utilizzabile' from 15 May 2026.
rows.notes: Italy's general SdI mandate dates from 1 January 2019; this row records only the final extension that pulled the smallest flat-rate taxpayers in. The 2019 general row and the 1 July 2022 cohort row are not yet recorded.

rows.regime_label: National e-Invoice System (KSeF — Krajowy System e-Faktur)
rows.bound_party: VAT taxpayers whose sales value including the tax amount exceeded PLN 200,000,000 in 2024.
rows.threshold_basis: Sales value including the tax amount (wartość sprzedaży wraz z kwotą podatku)
rows.threshold_period: calendar year 2024 — a fixed historical year, not a rolling period
rows.threshold_definition: The portal gates the first phase on sales exceeding "200 mln zł" in 2024. Because the reference year is fixed at 2024, a company cannot fall out of this phase by shrinking in 2025: whoever was above the line in 2024 is in the February cohort permanently.
rows.format_name: FA (KSeF structured invoice schema)
rows.format_note: FA_RR(1) applies to agricultural invoices from April 2026.
rows.legal_instrument: Ustawa z dnia 5 sierpnia 2025 r. o zmianie ustawy o podatku od towarów i usług (Dz. U. 2025 poz. 1203).
rows.source_title: "Podstawy prawne oraz kluczowe terminy" — legal basis and key dates, Ministry of Finance KSeF portal (ksef.podatki.gov.pl)
rows.confidence_note: Read directly on 2026-10-07: the 1 February 2026 date, the PLN 200 million threshold, the 2024 reference year, and the citing act Dz. U. 2025 poz. 1203.
unknowns: Whether the PLN 200m test is measured on taxable sales only or on total sales including exempt supplies is not specified on the portal page read.
rows.notes: The February cohort is small in number but includes most large Polish groups and their suppliers' counterparties, so it drives supplier readiness well ahead of April.

rows.regime_label: National e-Invoice System (KSeF — Krajowy System e-Faktur)
rows.bound_party: All remaining VAT taxpayers — those whose 2024 sales value including the tax amount did not exceed PLN 200,000,000.
rows.threshold_basis: Sales value including the tax amount (wartość sprzedaży wraz z kwotą podatku)
rows.threshold_period: calendar year 2024 — a fixed historical year, not a rolling period
rows.threshold_definition: The residual cohort: everyone not caught by the PLN 200 million 2024 test. The portal describes this phase as "all remaining entrepreneurs" from 1 April 2026, subject to the PLN 10,000/month small-invoice transition recorded in tolerance_ends.
rows.format_name: FA (KSeF structured invoice schema)
rows.format_note: FA_RR(1) applies to agricultural invoices from April 2026.
rows.tolerance_note: Small-invoice transition running to 31 December 2026. A taxpayer otherwise obliged to issue structured invoices may still issue electronic or paper invoices in a given month where the total value of sales including tax documented by those invoices is PLN 10,000 or less. Cash registers and fiscal receipts bearing the purchaser's NIP — treated as simplified invoices, up to PLN 450 or EUR 100 — also remain usable to 31 December 2026, as does the deferral of the duty to quote KSeF numbers in B2B payments.
rows.legal_instrument: Ustawa z dnia 5 sierpnia 2025 r. o zmianie ustawy o podatku od towarów i usług (Dz. U. 2025 poz. 1203).
rows.source_title: "Podstawy prawne oraz kluczowe terminy" — legal basis and key dates, Ministry of Finance KSeF portal (ksef.podatki.gov.pl)
rows.confidence_note: Read directly on 2026-10-07: the 1 April 2026 date for remaining taxpayers, and the PLN 10,000 monthly small-invoice transition expiring at the end of 2026.
unknowns: Whether the PLN 10,000 monthly test is applied per month independently (so a taxpayer can move in and out of the transition month to month) or is forfeited permanently once breached is not stated on the portal page read.
rows.notes: Out of scope per the portal: B2C invoices (voluntary), foreign entities with no Polish seat or fixed establishment, invoices under OSS, IOSS and the SME exemption, certain transport and toll services, and self-invoicing where a party lacks a Polish NIP.

rows.regime_label: National e-Invoice System (KSeF — Krajowy System e-Faktur)
rows.bound_party: All VAT taxpayers in Poland, regardless of size.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test. The Ministry of Finance states receiving via KSeF is mandatory from 1 February 2026 "regardless of company size", which is two months before the small-taxpayer issuing duty starts.
rows.format_name: FA (KSeF structured invoice schema)
rows.format_note: FA(3) is the logical structure for standard invoices. A separate FA_RR(1) structure applies to agricultural invoices from April 2026.
rows.legal_instrument: Ustawa z dnia 5 sierpnia 2025 r. o zmianie ustawy o podatku od towarów i usług (Dz. U. 2025 poz. 1203), amending the Polish VAT Act.
rows.source_title: "Zakres obowiązkowego KSeF" — scope of the mandatory KSeF obligation, Ministry of Finance KSeF portal (ksef.podatki.gov.pl)
rows.confidence_note: Read directly on 2026-10-07 on the Ministry of Finance KSeF portal, which states "Receiving invoices using KSeF will be mandatory already from 1 February 2026" for all VAT taxpayers, and names FA(3) as the current logical structure.
unknowns: Whether a taxpayer relying on the PLN 10,000/month small-invoice transition for ISSUING is nonetheless obliged to receive via KSeF from 1 February 2026 is not stated in terms. Read literally the receiving duty is unconditional, but the interaction is not spelled out on the portal.
rows.notes: The asymmetry here is the commercially important fact: a small Polish company is in scope for receiving on 1 February 2026, two months before the headline "April 2026" issuing date that most summaries lead with.

rows.regime_label: PT electronic invoicing — authenticity and integrity conditions
rows.bound_party: Taxable persons who issue invoices or other fiscally relevant documents by electronic means. Electronic issuing is itself optional in Portugal and requires the recipient's acceptance (art. 12.º n.º 1 of Decreto-Lei n.º 28/2019: the documents "podem, mediante aceitação pelo destinatário, ser emitidos por via eletrónica"). This row records the conditions that attach to an invoice once it IS issued electronically — not an obligation to stop using paper.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test of any kind. Portugal does not band this rule by turnover, headcount or entity type: it binds any taxable person who issues electronically, from a sole trader upwards. The condition is on HOW the invoice is issued, not on how big the issuer is. (Portugal's one size-banded e-invoicing rule is the B2G mandate under Decreto-Lei n.º 111-B/2017, which is a different counterparty scope and is not recorded as a row in v1 — see unknowns.)
rows.format_note: No structured format is mandated for B2B invoicing in Portugal — there is no CIUS, no UBL profile and no Peppol requirement on the B2B side. What art. 12.º n.º 2 of Decreto-Lei n.º 28/2019 requires instead is one of three authenticity-and-integrity procedures, read verbatim from the gazette: (a) "aposição de uma assinatura eletrónica qualificada nos termos legais"; (b) "aposição de um selo eletrónico qualificado, nos termos do Regulamento (UE) n.º 910/2014"; (c) "utilização de um sistema de intercâmbio eletrónico de dados" under an agreement following the European model EDI agreement (Recomendação n.º 1994/820/CE). A plain PDF file satisfies none of those three and is accepted only under the transitional rule in tolerance_ends. CIUS-PT and UBL 2.1 belong to the B2G regime, not to this row.
rows.tolerance_note: Lei n.º 73-A/2025 (Orçamento do Estado para 2026), art. 95.º n.º 3, verbatim: "Até 31 de dezembro de 2026 são aceites faturas em ficheiro PDF, sendo consideradas como faturas eletrónicas para todos os efeitos previstos na legislação fiscal." So until 2026-12-31 a plain PDF counts as an electronic invoice for every tax purpose, with none of the art. 12.º n.º 2 procedures applied. The tolerance is the PDF file itself, not a penalty holiday.
rows.legal_instrument: Lei n.º 73-A/2025, de 30 de dezembro (Orçamento do Estado para 2026), artigo 95.º n.º 3 ("Disposições transitórias relativas a obrigações fiscais"); Decreto-Lei n.º 28/2019, de 15 de fevereiro, artigos 6.º e 12.º ("Emissão de fatura por via eletrónica").
rows.source_title: Lei n.º 73-A/2025, de 30 de dezembro — Orçamento do Estado para 2026, Diário da República, 1.ª série, n.º 250, 2.º Suplemento, 30-12-2025 (files.dre.pt)
rows.confidence_note: Both instruments retrieved as the official Diário da República PDFs from files.dre.pt on 2026-10-07 and text-extracted. Art. 95.º n.º 3 of Lei n.º 73-A/2025 was read verbatim (see tolerance_note) in the 2.º Suplemento to DR n.º 250 of 30-12-2025. Art. 12.º n.os 1 and 2 of Decreto-Lei n.º 28/2019 were read verbatim in DR 1.ª série n.º 33 of 15-02-2019. The 2026-12-31 end of PDF acceptance is printed in the statute. The 2027-01-01 mandatory_from is the day after that printed cut-off — the complement of an explicit end-date, not a computed period, which is why this is graded verified where Spain's computed dates are not. What the statute does NOT say anywhere is that electronic invoicing becomes compulsory: see notes.
unknowns: Whether the PDF cut-off will be extended again. It sits in the annual budget law as a transitional provision, and art. 260.º of the same law prorogues a long list of other regimes by one year, so annual extension is clearly the mechanism. The extension history was not traced back through earlier budget laws this cycle, so how many times it has already moved is not established here. Treat 2027-01-01 as the current statutory position, not a settled one.

The AT's own administrative view on an invoice issued electronically on or after 2027-01-01 as a plain PDF — whether it is void, merely not an "electronic invoice", or treated some third way — was not read. No ofício circulado on the point was located this cycle. Ofício Circulado n.º 25120 of 2026-07-28 was retrieved and read and does not address it.

Portugal's B2G e-invoicing mandate is NOT recorded as a row. Art. 260.º n.º 2 of Lei n.º 73-A/2025 was read and prorogues "o regime previsto no n.º 4 do artigo 9.º do Decreto-Lei n.º 111-B/2017, de 31 de agosto" to 31 de dezembro de 2026 — which puts the remaining B2G cohort at 2027-01-01 — but the text of that art. 9.º n.º 4 was not itself retrieved, so exactly which cohort it covers is not confirmed here. v1 carries only the `e-invoicing-b2b` regime, so there is no slug for it either. Absence is not "no obligation".

Portugal's non-medium-specific invoicing duties — AT-certified billing software, the ATCUD unique document code, the QR code, and the SAF-T (PT) billing file — are reported by secondary sources to apply to every invoice whether paper, PDF or structured. None of them was verified this cycle and none is recorded as a row.
rows.notes: Read this row as a conditions row, not a mandate row. Portugal has no B2B obligation to issue electronic invoices at all: art. 12.º n.º 1 of Decreto-Lei n.º 28/2019 makes electronic issuing permissive and conditions it on the recipient's acceptance, so paper stays lawful and there is no receiving obligation to record either. The dated thing a buyer must act on is narrower and easy to miss: if you send PDF invoices to Portuguese customers, 2026-12-31 is the last day a bare PDF counts as an electronic invoice, and from 2027-01-01 it needs a qualified electronic signature, a qualified electronic seal, or an EDI arrangement. One adjacent date was read in the same article and is worth knowing: art. 95.º n.º 2 defers the SAF-T (PT) accounting file to tax periods from 2027 onwards, filed in 2028 or later.

rows.regime_label: RO e-Factura — national electronic invoicing system
rows.bound_party: Economic operators established in Romania issuing invoices in B2B relationships to taxable persons established in Romania under art. 266(2) of the Fiscal Code.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test on the obligation itself. Size only affects the penalty tariff: ANAF sets fines of RON 5,000–10,000 for large taxpayers, RON 2,500–5,000 for medium taxpayers and RON 1,000–2,500 for other legal persons and for individuals.
rows.format_note: Format not recorded. Romania uses a national CIUS of EN 16931 (commonly cited as RO_CIUS), but neither the format name nor its version was confirmed from a source read this cycle: the OUG 120/2021 PDF on mfinante.gov.ro reset the connection and the ANAF schema PDF was not retrieved. Recording a format name without having read it would be exactly the half-fact this dataset exists to avoid.
rows.legal_instrument: OUG nr. 120/2021 privind administrarea, funcționarea și implementarea sistemului național privind factura electronică RO e-Factura, as amended and supplemented by OUG nr. 115/2023, art. 10(1), art. 13^1 and art. 13^2; Legea nr. 296/2023 art. LIX(7); Legea nr. 227/2015 (Codul Fiscal) art. 319(16).
rows.source_title: ANAF, "Termenele legale de transmitere a facturii electronice în sistemul național RO e-factura" — Administrația Județeană a Finanțelor Publice Vrancea, DGRFP Galați (anaf.ro)
rows.confidence_note: ANAF notice retrieved as PDF and text-extracted on 2026-10-07. It states that from 01.07.2024 an issuer's failure to transmit the invoice into RO e-Factura, and a recipient's receipt and recording of a B2B invoice from a Romanian-established operator without compliance with art. 10(1), is penalised at 15% of the total invoice value. That 15% sanction on non-transmission from 1 July 2024 is what makes the system mandatory rather than merely available, which is why this row's mandatory_from is 2024-07-01.
unknowns: Invoice format name and version (RO_CIUS / EN 16931) not confirmed from a source read.
Whether the obligation extends to non-established but Romanian-VAT-registered suppliers is not recorded.
B2G e-invoicing in Romania predates the B2B regime and is not yet a row.
rows.notes: Transmission deadline: 5 working days from invoice issue and no later than 5 working days from the art. 319(16) Fiscal Code issuing deadline; from 1 July 2024 this became 5 CALENDAR days rather than working days. The working-day to calendar-day switch on the same date as the mandate is an easy detail to miss and materially tightens the duty.

rows.regime_label: RO e-Factura — national electronic invoicing system
rows.bound_party: Economic operators — taxable persons established in Romania — during the initial reporting phase, required to report all invoices into the RO e-Factura system.
rows.threshold_basis: Taxable persons established in Romania
rows.threshold_definition: The transitional phase of the Romanian mandate: from 1 January 2024 all invoices had to be reported into RO e-Factura, ahead of the full 1 July 2024 mandate under which non-transmission itself became a 15%-of-invoice-value offence.
rows.format_note: Format not recorded — see RO-e-invoicing-b2b-issue-all.
rows.tolerance_note: Penalty tolerance only. ANAF: failure to meet the transmission deadline in the B2B relationship was not sanctioned as a contravention in the period 1 January – 31 March 2024. The reporting duty itself ran from 1 January 2024; only the fine was withheld.
rows.legal_instrument: OUG nr. 120/2021, as amended by OUG nr. 115/2023; Legea nr. 296/2023 art. LIX(7); Legea nr. 227/2015 (Codul Fiscal) art. 319(16).
rows.source_title: ANAF, "Termenele legale de transmitere a facturii electronice în sistemul național RO e-factura" — DGRFP Galați / AJFP Vrancea (anaf.ro)
rows.confidence_note: ANAF notice read on 2026-10-07, which states the contravention tolerance for the B2B relationship over 1 January – 31 March 2024 and the 5-working-day then 5-calendar-day transmission deadlines.
unknowns: The exact commencement instrument and date for the reporting phase were taken from the tolerance window's framing rather than from the ordinance text, which was not retrieved (mfinante.gov.ro connection reset).
rows.notes: Retained as a historical row rather than deleted. The change log is a product: a buyer reconstructing what was required of them in Q1 2024 needs this row, and it is also the cleanest worked example in the dataset of a tolerance that withheld penalties without postponing the duty.

rows.regime_label: SK eFaktúra — mandatory structured e-invoicing under § 85o of the VAT Act
rows.bound_party: A VAT payer under § 4, § 4b or § 4c of the VAT Act (i.e. registered Slovak VAT payers, including VAT groups) which, on or after 1 January 2027, supplies goods or services to a person listed in § 85o(3) — § 85o(2).
rows.threshold_basis: VAT payer registered under § 4, § 4b or § 4c of zákon č. 222/2004 Z. z.
rows.threshold_definition: No turnover or headcount threshold in § 85o. The test is VAT-payer status: registration under § 4, § 4b or § 4c. A taxable person below the Slovak VAT registration threshold and not voluntarily registered is therefore outside the issuing duty — which makes this a LIVE entity-class test, not a dead one, and the reason the Slovak VAT registration threshold itself becomes a compliance variable. That threshold figure was not read and is named in unknowns rather than guessed.
rows.format_name: Structured electronic format conforming to the European standard
rows.format_note: § 85o(4) requires the invoice to be in "formáte elektronického dokumentu, ktorý umožňuje jeho automatizované a elektronické spracovanie" and "v dátovej štruktúre v súlade s technickou normou", with the technical norm carried by a cross-reference ("osobitný predpis") rather than named inline in the provision read. That cross-reference was not resolved to a specific standard and version, so no version is recorded. Secondary sources state the standard is EN 16931 and that the exchange runs on a Peppol five-corner model via a "doručovacia služba" (delivery service); the Peppol claim in particular is NOT confirmed against the Act or the Financial Administration and is recorded only in unknowns.
rows.legal_instrument: Zákon č. 222/2004 Z. z. o dani z pridanej hodnoty, § 85o(2) and § 85o(4), as inserted by zákon č. 385/2025 Z. z.; effectiveness under čl. VIII of act 385/2025. Act 385/2025 transposes Council Directive (EU) 2025/516.
rows.source_title: Zákon č. 385/2025 Z. z., consolidated text as in force from 1 January 2027 — slov-lex, the official legislative portal of the Slovak Republic
rows.confidence_note: Consolidated statutory text read on slov-lex on 2026-10-07. § 85o(2) binds a "platiteľ podľa § 4, 4b alebo § 4c, ktorý počnúc 1. januárom 2027 dodal osobe..." — the 2027-01-01 date is in the operative provision itself, not only in the commencement article. Čl. VIII provides "Tento zákon nadobúda účinnosť 1. januára 2026 okrem..." with the e-invoicing and reporting provisions effective 2027-01-01 and the cross-border extension 2030-07-01.
unknowns: The "osobitný predpis" technical-norm cross-reference in § 85o(4) was not resolved, so the format standard and its version are not established. EN 16931 is the likely referent but was not confirmed, and no version can be recorded.
Whether the exchange is legally required to run over Peppol, or whether Peppol is merely the expected implementation of the "doručovacia služba", is not established.

Secondary sources report a Ministry of Finance grace period for the first quarter of 2027. No such transitional provision was found in the text read, so tolerance_ends is left null rather than recorded. A tolerance that cannot be located in the instrument must not be sold as a date.
The Slovak VAT registration threshold — which decides who is inside this entity-class test — was not read.
Slovakia's pre-existing B2G e-invoicing position (the IS EFA / Informačný systém elektronickej fakturácie) is not yet a row.
rows.notes: § 85o(21)–(22) provide a voluntary on-ramp during 2026: e-invoicing via the delivery service may be used before the mandate, and recipient consent is not required where the recipient accepts the delivery service. That is the opposite of a tolerance — it is permission to start early, and it is why 2026 is a migration year in Slovakia rather than a grace year.

rows.regime_label: SK eFaktúra — mandatory structured e-invoicing under § 85o of the VAT Act
rows.bound_party: Persons listed in § 85o(3): a taxable person with its seat, place of business or establishment in Slovakia, and a non-taxable legal person with its seat in Slovakia.
rows.threshold_basis: Taxable person or non-taxable legal person with a seat, place of business or establishment in Slovakia (§ 85o(3))
rows.threshold_definition: No size test. The receiving side is defined by establishment in Slovakia rather than by VAT registration, so it is WIDER than the issuing side: a non-VAT-registered Slovak taxable person, and a non-taxable Slovak legal person, must be able to receive an eFaktúra from 2027-01-01 even though neither has a duty to issue one. Same asymmetry as Croatia, and the same trap.
rows.format_name: Structured electronic format conforming to the European standard
rows.format_note: Same format duty and same unresolved technical-norm cross-reference as the issuing row — see SK-e-invoicing-b2b-issue-vat-payer.
rows.legal_instrument: Zákon č. 222/2004 Z. z., § 85o(3), as inserted by zákon č. 385/2025 Z. z.; effectiveness under čl. VIII of act 385/2025.
rows.source_title: Zákon č. 385/2025 Z. z., consolidated text as in force from 1 January 2027 — slov-lex
rows.confidence_note: § 85o(3) read on slov-lex on 2026-10-07: "zdaniteľná osoba, ktorá má v tuzemsku sídlo, miesto podnikania..." and "nezdaniteľná právnická osoba, ktorá má v tuzemsku sídlo...". The 2027-01-01 date comes from § 85o(2) and čl. VIII.
unknowns: Format standard and version not established — same unresolved cross-reference as the issuing row.
Whether a recipient must register with a delivery service by a specific date, and what happens to an issuer whose recipient has not, is not recorded.
rows.notes: Recorded separately because the obligor population differs from the issuing row. Sizing the Slovak market off the VAT-payer count alone would undercount the businesses that have to implement something by 2027-01-01.

rows.regime_label: SK oznamovanie údajov — digital reporting of invoice data to the Financial Administration
rows.bound_party: All taxable persons, for cross-border supplies of goods and services, under the ViDA-aligned extension of the e-invoicing and digital reporting duties.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test, and no VAT-payer gate: this phase reaches all taxable persons, which is wider than the 2027 domestic phase. It follows the Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 timetable rather than a Slovak policy choice.
rows.format_name: Structured electronic format conforming to the European standard
rows.format_note: Same unresolved technical-norm cross-reference as the domestic rows. The consolidated text read was the version in force 2027-01-01 to 2030-06-30, so the wording governing the 2030-07-01 phase was not itself read.
rows.legal_instrument: Zákon č. 222/2004 Z. z. as amended by zákon č. 385/2025 Z. z., effectiveness under čl. VIII; Council Directive (EU) 2025/516.
rows.source_title: Zákon č. 385/2025 Z. z., consolidated text as in force from 1 January 2027 — slov-lex
rows.confidence_note: The 2030-07-01 cross-border date appears in the commencement structure of act 385/2025 (čl. VIII) and in the slov-lex validity range of the text read, which is stated as 2027-01-01 to 2030-06-30. But the provisions that take effect on 2030-07-01 were NOT read — a consolidated text in force from 2027 does not contain them. Graded reported rather than verified for that reason: the date is sound, the obligation's wording is not yet sourced.
unknowns: The operative provisions effective 2030-07-01 have not been read. The slov-lex consolidated text for that date needs to be fetched separately before this row can be graded verified.

§ 85o(18)–(19) defer some delivery-service-provider reporting under §§ 80–80a to 2030-06-30, and secondary sources describe a deferral of BUYER-side digital reporting to July 2030. Whether there is a distinct recipient-side reporting obligation starting in 2030 was not established, so no receive-direction reporting row is recorded.
rows.notes: Recorded now because a 2030 date four years out is exactly what a compliance buyer is trying to budget for, but graded honestly: this is a commencement date read from the amending act, not an obligation read from the text that will be in force.

rows.regime_label: SK oznamovanie údajov — digital reporting of invoice data to the Financial Administration
rows.bound_party: The issuer of an electronic invoice, obliged to transmit the prescribed invoice data to the Financial Administration via the delivery service (doručovacia služba) — § 85o(9) and § 85o(11).
rows.threshold_basis: VAT payer registered under § 4, § 4b or § 4c of zákon č. 222/2004 Z. z.
rows.threshold_definition: No size test beyond VAT-payer status, which is the same gate as the issuing duty it rides on.
rows.format_name: § 74(1) and § 68d(4) invoice data set, transmitted via the doručovacia služba
rows.format_note: The Act prescribes the data by cross-reference to § 74(1) and § 68d(4) of the VAT Act rather than naming a versioned published schema. The Financial Administration's technical specification was not read, so no version is recorded.
rows.legal_instrument: Zákon č. 222/2004 Z. z., § 85o(9) and § 85o(11), as inserted by zákon č. 385/2025 Z. z.
rows.source_title: Zákon č. 385/2025 Z. z., consolidated text as in force from 1 January 2027 — slov-lex
rows.confidence_note: § 85o(9) read on slov-lex on 2026-10-07 and sets the reporting deadline as "do piatich dní odo dňa vyhotovenia elektronickej faktúry" — five days from the date the electronic invoice is drawn up. § 85o(11) routes it "prostredníctvom doručovacej služby". Data scope is cross-referenced to § 74(1) and § 68d(4).
unknowns: Whether the five-day deadline runs in calendar or working days was not established from the text read. Romania changed exactly this parameter mid-mandate, so it matters.
The technical schema and version for the reported data set are not established.
rows.notes: Five days from drawing up the invoice is a reporting window, not real time — materially easier to implement than Hungary's immediate RTIR or Italy's clearance model, and worth saying plainly because buyers often assume every new mandate is real-time.
